name: call_library_jump_vectors
description: Program entry that calls a library function through a global base pointer, then makes two calls through the pointer that call returned and one more through the global base, and returns zero. The facts show exec OpenLibrary and CloseLibrary calls and the text dos.library, which point to opening dos.library.

name: unpack_compressed_stream_to_memory
description: Copies a block of packed data into a buffer, then reads bits to choose between copying a run of bytes from earlier in the output and emitting literal bytes, looping until the output pointer reaches a fixed limit. The facts list a write to the COLOR00 colour register and calls to bit-reading routines.

name: refill_bit_buffer_word
description: Reads a 32-bit word from memory just before the current input position, stores its low byte through the output pointer, and returns that word shifted right by one with the top bit set. Its shape matches the refill the unpacking routine calls whenever its bit buffer runs empty.

name: shift_bit_buffer_count
description: Shifts a bit buffer right by a count held in a register, calling the refill routine whenever the buffer runs out, and then returns.

name: chain_two_routine_calls
description: Four-instruction routine whose decompiled code timed out, so only its facts are known: it calls two other routines. Its purpose cannot be read from the listing.

name: copy_365_longs_to_buffer
description: Copies 365 longs from a data block into a fixed low-memory buffer with a counted loop, then returns zero. The facts show it is called by find_max_and_prepare_buffer.

name: configure_dma_and_interrupts
description: Writes the colour, DMA control and interrupt enable registers, then calls one other routine; the decompiler timed out, so the exact values are not shown. The register notes say writes with the top bit set enable DMA channels or interrupts and writes without it disable them.

name: setup_plot_boot_dma
description: Refers to the text PLOT.BOOT and writes to the DMA control register, then calls two other routines. The decompiled code is unavailable, so only the referenced text and the register use are known.

name: copy_1001_longs_and_reset
description: Sets a bit in a global flag word, calls a routine, then copies 1001 longs from a data block into a fixed low-memory table, writes a constant to a global word twice and xors a shared word with a constant. The facts list the CIA-A port A register as touched, which carries the fire-button and disk-status lines.

name: disable_all_interrupts_and_dma
description: Writes a value with every bit except the top one set to the interrupt enable and DMA control registers, twice, then xors a shared word with a fixed constant. The register notes say writes without the top bit disable interrupts and DMA channels, so this switches them off.

name: lookup_uppercased_name_in_table
description: Copies a text argument into a buffer converting lowercase letters to uppercase, derives a slot number by hashing the length and characters modulo 72, then walks the table entries in that slot comparing the name with each record. It sets a status value when no entry or no match is found, and copies the matched record's data out when one is found.

name: lookup_entry_by_fixed_hash
description: Computes a slot number by hashing a fixed run of bytes that starts near its own code, then walks the table entries in that slot, comparing names and copying a matched record out. A missing or mismatched entry sets a status value instead.

name: find_record_at_slot
description: Takes a slot index, reads the first entry from the table at that slot, and walks the chain comparing the requested name with each stored name. It sets a status value for not-found or mismatched results, copies the matched record out, and calls several routines.

name: set_status_six_then_exit
description: Sets a status word in the lookup context to 6, then calls one routine and returns.

name: set_status_seven_then_exit
description: Sets a status word in the lookup context to 7, then calls one routine and returns.

name: match_text_then_copy_record
description: Compares a text argument byte by byte against a stored name, and on a full match copies the record out; when the comparison fails it sets a status value and calls the record-copy routine. It loops through records until one matches.

name: scan_records_for_key
description: Walks records one at a time, checks a count field in each, and compares a stored key with a fixed text. A matching record has its data copied out, and failed checks set status values 5, 6 or 7 and return.

name: copy_record_bytes_to_buffer
description: Copies a record's stored bytes into the output buffer in a loop driven by a length field and a counter, and sets a status value if the first check fails. It calls several routines and then returns.

name: copy_record_payload_loop
description: Repeatedly copies a fixed-length payload from a record into the output buffer, advancing the output pointer and stopping when a counter goes negative. It calls a routine on each pass, and it writes the final output pointer back to the lookup context.

name: set_status_one_then_exit
description: Sets the status word in the lookup context to 1, then calls one routine and returns.

name: verify_table_checksum
description: Temporarily zeroes one stored word, sums the negated 128 longs of the table, restores the word, and returns zero when the sum equals the saved value or minus one otherwise. It is a checksum verification over a table block.

name: set_status_five_then_exit
description: Sets the status word in the lookup context to 5, then calls one routine and returns.

name: retry_position_lookup
description: Splits a stored 16-bit value into a quotient and remainder by 22, adjusts the remainder and a side flag, then calls routines in a loop until a call reports success or a limit of five attempts is reached.

name: retry_nested_operation_limits
description: Clears a result word, then calls a routine to run an operation and retries it while counting failures, with an outer loop that repeats the whole attempt up to five times and saves intermediate values between tries. When every retry is used up it sets error status 2 and returns the result of its last call.

name: retry_operation_five_times
description: Repeats a routine call up to five times per pass across five passes, saving the position on each failed attempt. When all passes fail it sets error status 2 and returns the last result.

name: reset_counters_store_position
description: Clears two retry counters and stores a position word built from two stored values, one of them multiplied by 128 and added to the other.

name: set_bit2_and_step_position
description: Sets bit 2 of a byte at a hardware address when a flag is non-zero and clears it otherwise, then calls a routine. It then calls a routine on each step while a position value moves toward a target, and clears a counter if it is negative.

name: clear_bit2_and_step_position
description: Clears bit 2 of a byte at a hardware address, then calls a routine. It then calls a routine on each step while a position value moves toward a target, and clears a counter if it is negative.

name: wait_until_position_reached
description: Calls a routine, then loops until a position value equals a target, calling a routine on each pass where the position is not yet at the target. It returns once the two values match.

name: wait_for_port_bit_clear
description: Calls a routine repeatedly while bit 4 of a byte at a hardware address stays set, then clears a counter word.

name: poll_port_bit_then_clear
description: Checks bit 4 of a byte at a hardware address and, while it is set, calls a routine and checks again. When the bit clears it zeroes a counter word and returns.

name: advance_counter_until_limit
description: Calls a routine and increments a counter word, repeating until the counter reaches 79.

name: advance_counter_below_limit
description: Checks whether a counter word is below 79 and, while it is, calls a routine and increments the counter.

name: clear_bit1_and_increment_counter
description: Clears bit 1 of a byte at a hardware address, calls a routine, then increments a counter word.

name: set_bit1_and_decrement_counter
description: Sets bit 1 of a byte at a hardware address, calls a routine, then decrements a counter word.

name: pulse_bit0_then_call_routine
description: Clears and then sets bit 0 of a byte at a hardware address, producing a pulse, then calls one routine and returns.

name: wait_on_vertical_beam_position
description: Busy-waits on the vertical beam position register with an empty loop body, reading that register twice per pass. The listed facts show only this register, and the decompiled test compares two readings, so the exact wait target is not clear from the listing.

name: wait_port_bit5_with_timeout
description: Polls bit 5 of a byte at a hardware address until it clears, giving up after a fixed large count of tries. On timeout it sets status 4 and calls the exit routine.

name: set_status_four_then_exit
description: Sets the status word in the lookup context to 4, then calls one routine and returns.

name: program_block_and_wait_ready
description: Writes a sequence of control values into a register block at fixed offsets from a base pointer, then waits up to a fixed count for a ready bit in a status word. If the ready bit never appears it sets status 3 and calls the exit routine; otherwise it writes a final value and returns.

name: write_control_word_bit14
description: Writes a control word with only bit 14 set to a register at a fixed offset from a base pointer, then returns.

name: decode_sector_after_sync_word
description: Scans a buffer for the standard Amiga disk sector sync word, then checks the sector header against expected values, and decodes 128 longs by combining odd and even bit fields under a mask. It returns zero on success and minus one when a header check fails.

name: find_matching_sector_and_decode
description: Scans forward for the Amiga disk sync word and then for a sector header with the wanted number, checks two further header values, and decodes 128 longs under a mask into the output. It returns zero on success and minus one when any check fails.

name: decode_sector_if_checks_match
description: Compares two values from the header and, if they agree, decodes 128 longs from the buffer into the output by combining odd and even bit fields under a mask. Otherwise it returns minus one.

name: decode_128_long_sector_block
description: Decodes 128 longs by merging each odd bit field with the adjacent even field under a mask, writes them to the output, clears a status counter and returns zero.

name: stub_return_failure_value
description: Returns minus one immediately with no other work. The facts show no calls and three unnamed callers, so it serves as a failure return for them.

name: stub_return_only
description: Returns immediately with no calls, memory access or hardware register use, so it does no work. The facts show it is referenced by address and called from routines.

name: compute_xor_checksum_run
description: XORs together a run of longs starting at a pointer, for a count held in a register, and returns the result masked with a value from another register. It is a checksum over the run.

name: pulse_ciab_port_bit3_low
description: Writes a value with every bit except the top one set to the CIA-B port B byte, calls a routine, clears bit 3, and calls another routine. The register is named in the facts, and bit 3 is driven low.

name: pulse_ciab_port_bit3_high
description: Sets bits 7 and 3 of the CIA-B port B byte, calls a routine, clears bit 3, calls another routine, then sets bit 3 again. Bit 3 is low only for the middle interval.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiled listing holds only a halt at bad instruction data, so no behaviour can be read from this entry. The facts say it is referenced by two unnamed routines.

name: stub_runtime_segment_data
description: This runtime memory segment of 14336 instructions has decompiled code that is only a halt at bad instruction data, so none of its routines can be recovered from the listing. It was reached by execution from outside the static flow.
